title: AI for small business: a practical implementation path
description: Build a grounded assistant, check a sales analysis, connect one customer workflow, and decide whether it is ready for a controlled pilot. Six modules combine worked tutorials, original practice files, knowledge checks, and an evidence-based capstone.
audience: Owners and small teams in services, retail, ecommerce, and creative businesses who can use a browser and a basic spreadsheet.
timeEstimate: Plan for roughly 7–13 hours of active practice, plus vendor setup and any real email delays. These are editorial planning estimates, not measured completion times.
credentialStatement: This is a self-study implementation path. It does not award an accredited qualification or independently assessed certificate.
progressStatement: Progress marks and knowledge-check answers are saved in this browser. They are your own record, not proof that a vendor workflow has passed its tests. Keep the underlying evidence in your own project folder.
prerequisites: Choose one small, repeatable business task and identify the person responsible for its output.
Be able to save a text file, open a CSV in a spreadsheet, and distinguish a draft from a sent message.
Use the supplied fictional records for practice. For a real pilot, have permission to use the information and remove unnecessary personal or confidential data.
Reading and downloading the materials requires no course account. Connected exercises need the vendor accounts and capabilities listed in each tutorial; check current limits before paying.
outcomes: Create a business facts file that separates approved facts, assumptions, and questions requiring a human answer.
Reconcile an AI-assisted sales analysis to an independent calculation, including duplicates, refunds, cancellations, and a missing cost.
Build either a confirmed lead-magnet delivery sequence or a service-inquiry workflow that prepares a reviewed draft.
Explain and test input validation, duplicate handling, failure recovery, source updates, and human escalation.
Assemble a portfolio that supports a specific go, revise, or stop decision for one controlled business pilot.
limitations: A knowledge-check score shows how you answered these questions; it does not verify your live accounts or business results.
The supplied examples are synthetic exercises. Vendor interface documentation and reference answers are distinguished from an observed run in your account.
Instructor feedback, external qualification, measured learner outcomes, and guaranteed time savings or traffic are not included.
howToUse: Work through the modules in order. In module 3, choose the track that matches your business; you do not need to build both.
Keep a project folder with a dated brief, source files, outputs, calculations, test log, and final decision. Store your own work there, not in a public comment or this site's progress controls.
Try each knowledge check before opening its explanation. A wrong answer points to the part to revisit; you can retry.
Mark a module complete only after its submission and pass criteria are satisfied. Label simulated practice separately from connected account tests.
Complete the capstone on one workflow. A decision to revise or stop is a useful result when the evidence does not justify launch.

modules.title: Choose one task and ground your assistant
modules.summary: Give the assistant reliable business facts and define what success would mean before asking it to produce work.
modules.timeEstimate: 35–60 minutes of active practice; editorial estimate.
objectives: Define one task, its owner, its input, and the output a person will approve.
Separate source-backed business facts from assumptions and missing information.
Check a generated FAQ and reply against the approved facts.

lessons.label: Choose the first task to automate
Build a ChatGPT Project business brief
Compare assistant fit and account requirements

submission: A one-page task brief: customer or colleague served, trigger, approved output, owner, excluded actions, and one quality measure.
A dated business facts file with a source or owner for each policy, price, turnaround, and contact detail used in the exercise.
One FAQ and one inquiry reply with a claim-check table: claim, source, supported or unsupported, and correction. Include one question that the sources cannot answer.
passCriteria: Every price, policy, timing, and availability claim in the final outputs is traceable to an approved source; unsupported claims have been removed or escalated.
The deliberately unanswered question produces an honest request for information or a human handoff, not an invented policy.
The task brief records a baseline method and a quality measure. If no baseline has been observed yet, it says 'not measured' instead of estimating a saving.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Your facts file says replies usually arrive within one business day. The assistant writes, 'We guarantee a reply in one hour.' What should you do?

choices.text: Keep it if another AI assistant agrees.
Replace it with the supported timing and record the unsupported claim in the check log.
Ask for a more confident tone and publish the result.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: A second model is not a source for your policy. The approved business fact controls the wording. Recording the failure also gives you a useful case to test after the instructions change.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: You want to know whether an AI-assisted reply process helps. Which comparison is most useful?

choices.text: Count how many words the assistant generates.
Ask the assistant how many hours it probably saved.
Record comparable tasks before and during the pilot, including drafting, review, corrections, and final accuracy.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: A faster first draft may create extra review work. Count the whole task and a quality measure, state the sample size, and avoid claiming a general improvement from a small or mismatched sample.

modules.title: Check AI analysis against the numbers
modules.summary: Use an intentionally messy fictional sales file to learn when a persuasive answer is numerically wrong.
modules.timeEstimate: 60–90 minutes of active practice; editorial estimate.
objectives: Distinguish a duplicate event from a legitimate refund on the same order.
Keep an unknown cost unresolved until the supplied owner confirmation supports a value.
Reproduce the answer key and write a decision memo that stays within the data.

lessons.label: Analyze a sales CSV with ChatGPT and verify the result
Compare your work with the independent answer key

submission: A cleaning log listing which rows were removed, excluded, retained, or corrected, with the reason for each decision.
A reconciled table of net sales and contribution using the tutorial's definitions, with spreadsheet formulas or the supplied independent verifier.
A short owner memo with one supported finding, one proposed next action, and at least two limits on what the sample can establish.
passCriteria: Remove only exact duplicate event IDs as instructed, retain legitimate refund events, and exclude cancelled orders under the exercise rules.
Do not replace a missing cost with zero or an AI guess. Record the supplied owner confirmation before completing that calculation.

Match the exercise answer key: 27 raw rows, 25 unique events, 23 retained events, $702.00 net sales, and $240.90 contribution after the confirmed missing cost. Explain any discrepancy before moving on.

The memo distinguishes contribution from full business profit, names omitted overhead, advertising, labor, and taxes, and does not infer causal marketing effects or forecasts from this small synthetic sample.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: A paid order and its later refund share an order ID but have different event IDs. What is the correct starting treatment?

choices.text: Keep both events and apply the exercise's signed sale and refund rules.
Delete the refund because order IDs must be unique.
Keep only the larger amount.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: The file records events, not one row per order. Deduplicating on order ID would erase a real refund and overstate the result. Use the stable event ID and the documented event rules.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: One fulfilled sale has no cost value. ChatGPT suggests using the average cost of other products. What belongs in your checked result?

choices.text: Use the average without a note because it is statistically reasonable.
Treat the missing cost as zero to finish the table.
Keep it unknown until the owner confirmation supplies the exercise value, and record the correction.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: An estimate is not an observed cost. This exercise provides a separate confirmation specifically so you can resolve the missing value with evidence. If a real business cannot resolve it, disclose the uncertainty instead of presenting a precise profit figure.

modules.title: Build one customer workflow
modules.summary: Choose email resource delivery or service-inquiry follow-up. Both tracks join several tools and require evidence that the customer receives the intended result.
modules.timeEstimate: 60–120 minutes of active practice for one track; editorial estimate. The email track also requires waiting through the configured delivery intervals.
objectives: Map a customer action through the connected tools to one useful output.
Identify what can run automatically and what needs a person's approval.
Test both the expected path and a meaningful exception with controlled records.

lessons.label: Track A: Canva resource and MailerLite welcome sequence
Track B: Tally inquiry, Google Sheets record, and Gmail draft

tracks.title: Track A — Deliver a useful resource by email
tracks.bestFor: Stores, creators, and service businesses that already have a useful resource and a permission-based signup offer.
submission: The finished resource, signup page, three messages, and a simple field-and-trigger map.
A dated test log using controlled addresses: confirmation, correct resource access while signed out, real delay timing, unsubscribe, and repeat signup.
passCriteria: The correct resource reaches a fresh confirmed subscriber and opens without the creator's signed-in access.
Unsubscribing after the first message prevents later sequence messages; a repeat signup behaves as the configured repeat-entry setting specifies.
The actual delay intervals are recorded, and the workflow fits the account's ongoing plan after any trial ends.

tracks.title: Track B — Prepare a service inquiry for review
tracks.bestFor: Consultants, local services, and small teams that receive inquiries and want a reviewable reply with a reliable intake record.
submission: A form, intake-sheet field map, approved reply template, and an identified review owner.
A dated log for a complete submission, an optional blank field, a repeated submission, and a paused or failed handoff.
passCriteria: A controlled inquiry produces the matching source record and a Gmail draft with the correct recipient and business facts.
The action creates a draft without sending a message; the owner can find it and review it.
Duplicate drafts and failed handoffs are reconciled against the source before replay or reply.

submission: Identify the chosen track and complete its submission requirements.
Save the trigger-to-output map, dated results, and corrections in your portfolio. Mark any unperformed account test as pending.
passCriteria: All pass criteria for the chosen track are met with observed results, not a screenshot of configuration alone.
No pending delay, unsubscribe, draft-versus-send, or delivery test is marked passed.
The workflow has a named owner and a documented manual route if an integration stops.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: A lead-magnet PDF opens for you but the subscriber gets a permission error. Which test would have caught this?

choices.text: Previewing the email in the editor.
Opening the delivered link as a controlled recipient while signed out of the creator account.
Asking an assistant whether the link looks correct.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: The creator's access does not establish the recipient's access. Verify the whole delivery path with a controlled recipient and the same permissions a real subscriber will have.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: The service-inquiry workflow is intended to prepare replies for review. Which action satisfies that requirement?

choices.text: Send the message immediately and notify the owner afterward.
Send it only when the AI calls its answer confident.
Create a draft, verify that no message was sent, and give the owner a way to find it.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Review must happen before the external action. A draft action and an observed no-send check make that boundary testable. Confidence wording is not permission to contact a customer.

modules.title: Make the workflow recoverable
modules.summary: Practice the parts that a successful first run does not prove: bad input, duplicate events, retries, and recovery.
modules.timeEstimate: 45–90 minutes of active practice; editorial estimate. Connected setup depends on a trusted source that can send the required private header.
objectives: Validate the fields required to produce a useful queue record.
Use a stable submission ID to recognize a retried event.
Reconcile source records before retrying a paused or failed run.

lessons.label: Build a protected lead-review queue in Make
Check whether Zapier or Make fits the workflow

submission: A field map with required fields, the source's stable submission ID, and the human review owner.
A test log for a valid event, wrong authentication key, missing or blank required data, an identical retry, a conflicting retry with the same ID, and a second distinct event.
A recovery note explaining how to find missing or duplicate records, pause safely, and replay only what is missing.
passCriteria: Invalid required data does not become an apparently complete approved record.
The guide's no-overwrite configuration rejects a repeated key while preserving the original record. A conflicting retry is flagged for review; a different valid ID is treated as a separate event.
The recovery note compares the source with the destination before replay. Private endpoint credentials are kept out of public pages, screenshots, and browser-side code.
modules.practiceMode: If the trusted source or required account capability is unavailable, work through the sample payloads and write the expected record after each event. Label that as a simulation; connected recovery tests remain pending for the capstone.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: A form provider retries the same submission after a timeout. Which identifier supports reliable duplicate detection?

choices.text: The original submission ID, preserved across retries.
A new random ID generated on every retry.
The customer's first name.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: The destination needs a stable identity for the event. A new ID makes a retry appear new, while a first name can merge unrelated people. The ID rule must match the source and the guide's storage behavior.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: The integration stopped for an hour, and some source submissions may already be in the queue. What should happen before replay?

choices.text: Replay every event with a fresh ID.
Compare source IDs with destination records, identify missing events, and retry with their original IDs.
Delete the queue and ask the assistant to reconstruct it.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Reconciliation tells you what actually failed. Preserving identities and replaying missing records avoids creating duplicates or losing evidence of work that already succeeded.

modules.title: Test support answers and human handoff
modules.summary: Build an approved support source, challenge the assistant with known and unknown questions, and prove that a person receives the handoff.
modules.timeEstimate: 3–5 focused hours of active practice; editorial estimate. Live inbox and availability tests require the relevant Tidio account capabilities.
objectives: Resolve conflicting policy sources before loading a knowledge base.
Score support answers for required facts, forbidden claims, and escalation behavior.
Prove online handoff, offline contact, and a usable rollback route.

lessons.label: Build and test a Tidio Lyro support knowledge base

submission: A source register with owner, effective date, active source, and the resolution of any stale or conflicting policy.
The supplied test log with observed responses, source support, pass or fail, and a corrective action for every mandatory case.
Evidence that a controlled handoff reaches the real destination, including offline handling and the manual contact path after rollback.
passCriteria: All 20 mandatory cases and five high-risk paraphrase retests meet their expected behavior, with zero critical failures. Blocked or unrun cases remain pending.
A connected online handoff and offline ticket reach the actual destination with usable context, and a human reply is verified on the visitor side.
No unresolved conflicting active source remains, and disabling the bot leaves a usable human contact route.
modules.practiceMode: You can score the fictional cases and diagnose the stale-policy problem without a live bot. These reference answers are not evidence of Lyro's observed behavior. Mark live response, inbox, and rollback tests pending until you perform them.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: An old returns page and an approved new FAQ contain different deadlines. What should you do before enabling support answers?

choices.text: Load both and let the assistant pick the more generous deadline.
Confirm the current policy with its owner, remove or correct the stale active source, and rerun the affected tests.
Use whichever deadline appeared in the first test response.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: The business owns the policy decision. Prompt wording cannot reliably repair conflicting source material. Resolve the source conflict, record the decision, then test the answers that depend on it.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: The chat widget says 'A person will follow up,' but no one has checked the support inbox. Has the handoff passed?

choices.text: Yes, because the visitor saw the right sentence.
Yes, if the bot answered the previous question correctly.
No. Confirm the request and necessary context arrived at the actual destination, including the offline route.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: A handoff is an operational event, not a reassuring phrase. The test is whether the responsible person can find the request and act on it under the availability conditions you promise.

modules.title: Present a pilot with evidence
modules.summary: Choose one workflow from your portfolio and produce a decision another person can inspect: what it does, what passed, what remains uncertain, and when it must stop.
modules.timeEstimate: 45–90 minutes to assemble the evidence and decision; editorial estimate. Collecting a real business baseline and running a pilot takes additional time.
objectives: Separate completed practice, connected tests, and live business outcomes.
Evaluate a pilot against explicit quality, cost, and recovery criteria.
Give an owner a repeatable procedure for using, reviewing, updating, and stopping the workflow.

lessons.label: Use the capstone rubric and evidence template below
Review the site's evidence and editorial standards

submission: An evidence pack containing the task brief, current sources, input and output examples, independent checks, dated test log, and owner procedure.
A measured baseline and pilot comparison for comparable tasks, or an explicit 'outcomes not yet measured' entry with the next measurement step.
A one-page decision: controlled pilot, revise, or stop; the reasons; unresolved limitations; operating cost assumptions; and the next review date.
passCriteria: The self-review rubric reaches at least 10 of 12 points, with no criterion scoring zero and no unresolved critical failure.
A proposed live pilot has completed the relevant connected delivery, approval, recovery, and escalation tests. Simulations alone support a practice-complete or revise decision.
Claims of improvement cite the observed sample and include review, correction, and tool costs. Missing business outcome evidence is clearly marked rather than replaced with a promise.
A named person accepts the operating procedure, stop conditions, source-update responsibility, and review date.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Nineteen support tests pass, but one invents a refund entitlement. Which decision follows the launch criteria?

choices.text: Launch because the average score is high.
Fix the critical failure and repeat the affected and regression tests before a live pilot.
Hide that test from the report because it is unusual.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: A serious failure is not cancelled out by unrelated successful answers. The pilot needs a defined stop rule, a correction, and evidence that the change fixed the problem without breaking previously correct behavior.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Five practice replies were faster with AI, but they used fictional messages and no customer follow-up. What is a defensible conclusion?

choices.text: The exercise supports a limited next test; it does not establish business-wide savings or better customer outcomes.
The business will save the same percentage on every future message.
The workflow is proven to increase revenue.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: State what the sample actually measured. Synthetic practice can expose mistakes and justify a controlled trial, but it does not measure customer response, long-term costs, or revenue effects.

capstone.title: Capstone: one workflow another person can inspect
capstone.reviewMethod: Score your evidence, not your intention. This is a self-review rubric created for this path, not an independently validated assessment. A colleague or owner can use the same rubric to challenge the decision.
capstone.passRule: At least 10/12, no zero, and no unresolved critical failure. A connected pilot also requires observed account tests. Record 'revise' if evidence is missing; do not convert a simulation into a live pass.

scores.1: Task, owner, output, and baseline method are defined; actual outcome measurement is explicitly pending.
scores.2: Comparable baseline observations and quality measures are recorded with sample size and limitations.

scores.0: Material facts are invented, untraceable, or in unresolved conflict.
scores.1: Sources and permission are recorded, with remaining noncritical gaps clearly excluded from the workflow.
scores.2: Every material fact is traceable to a current approved source with an owner and update rule.

scores.0: The evidence relies only on an AI's confidence or another model agreeing.
scores.1: Required outputs were checked against the tutorial's reference or an approved source, and discrepancies are logged.
scores.2: Checks reproduce the result independently and include meaningful boundary or exception cases.

scores.0: Critical delivery, duplicate, approval, or handoff behavior is untested or fails.
scores.1: Practice tests and an executable connected-test plan exist, with unperformed tests explicitly marked pending.
scores.2: Relevant connected normal, exception, retry, and human-handoff tests have dated observed evidence.

scores.0: Savings, profit, or reliability claims exceed the evidence.
scores.1: Plan constraints, review work, and uncertainties are explicit; no unsupported business result is claimed.
scores.2: Observed time, correction effort, and applicable tool costs support a bounded comparison and a specific next decision.

scores.0: No person owns review, updates, or stopping the workflow.
scores.1: An owner, operating procedure, stop rule, and review date are written down.
scores.2: The owner can follow the procedure, explain a recovery, and document a completed correction and retest.

criticalFailures: An output invents a material price, policy, entitlement, availability, or account-specific fact.
The workflow performs an external action before a required human approval.
The process exposes private information or publicizes an integration secret.
A required delivery, unsubscribe, duplicate-control, recovery, or support-handoff test fails.
A result marked as observed was only simulated, predicted, or copied from the reference answer.

workedDecision.label: Illustrative decision, not a measured business result
workedDecision.scenario: A service-inquiry exercise creates the correct draft from a controlled form submission, but the paused-integration recovery test has not been run.
workedDecision.reason: The normal path has evidence, but missing-inquiry recovery is still pending. Run the pause, reconciliation, and replay test; record whether the correct draft appears without duplicates; then reassess the operating criterion. Do not claim time savings before measuring review and correction work.
